To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multi-user editing server can be designed that supports the editing of continuous media by multiple simultaneous editors, each of which is provided with continuous playback of the content being edited.
the system must support a large number of concurrent users, and the system must be able to support the concurrent display of the content for all users.
the system must support a shared storage model for the media content and that the shared storage must be a single disk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to support continuous display of edited content to multiple editors, and how to compute the set of proposed changes to this content.
how to support multiple editors in a post production environment.
the design of a system to allow multiple editors to work simultaneously on the same content, while supporting continuous display of the content for each editor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of a multi-user server requires careful consideration of the physical architecture, and that this architecture should be based on the specific needs of the intended users.
the system is a distributed, multi-processor, shared memory system that is capable of supporting multiple simultaneous editors.

the system design should support the following: 1) the ability to edit multiple copies of the same content, and 2) the ability to compute and compare the set of changes proposed by multiple editors in a timely fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a system that supports multiple editors in the same post production facility to edit the same content concurrently.
the design of multi-user editing systems is not just about the software that supports the editing process but also about the physical design of such systems.
the system design should provide a mechanism for each user to be able to edit the content in isolation from other users while maintaining the capability to share the content among all users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multi-user editing server should be built around a shared storage device, and that the storage device needs to be able to support multiple concurrent accesses from multiple editing clients.
the physical design of a multi-user editing server has a significant impact on the overall performance of the system.
a server that is optimized for a single editor will not be able to scale to support multiple editors.
